nodes.label: SLOOP firmware
nodes.rationale: Free open-source GPL-3.0 firmware for the M-VAVE FM-1; projects from 2.7 load unchanged in 2.8 and vice versa for compatibility.

nodes.label: Felucca (base firmware)
nodes.rationale: SLOOP is based on Felucca by Leo Kuroshita / Hugelton Instruments; many features are ported 'after Felucca' versions.

nodes.label: What's new in 2.8
nodes.rationale: Most 2.8 changes come from user comments and reports.

nodes.label: Install and update
nodes.rationale: Installer checks SHA-256 and the update loader checks CRC so a damaged package is refused before anything is written.

nodes.label: Four tracks (3 synth, 1 drum)
nodes.rationale: Track colour is shared with the knob of the same colour; white means what you touch, red means recording.

nodes.label: Tap and hold (two lives of a button)
nodes.rationale: Every function button has two lives: tap opens pages, hold opens a layer; layer screen appears after 0.35 s (2.8.3) so a quick tap no longer flashes it.

nodes.label: Lock a layer open
nodes.rationale: Locking a layer frees both hands: one on the keys, one on the knobs.

nodes.label: Levels (GHOST, SOFT, NORM, HARD)
nodes.rationale: The FM-1 keys have no velocity, so hits get one of four levels chosen with OCT- / OCT+.

nodes.label: Drum voice allocation (6 voices, kick last)
nodes.rationale: 2.8.3: a hit takes the voice of its own sound or the oldest voice, the kick last, so on a busy beat the kick no longer drops out.

nodes.label: Drum kits
nodes.rationale: Every kit is level-matched; changing the kit never touches the pattern.

nodes.label: DRUMS Sound page (per-sound TUNE / DECAY)
nodes.rationale: 2.8: TUNE also shapes brightness of tone-less sounds (hats, shakers, claps) that have no pitch to shift.

nodes.label: DRUM PREVIEW setting
nodes.rationale: OFF by default so picking a drum sound with a knob is silent, quiet for live.

nodes.label: Drum MUTE mode (EDIT + black key)
nodes.rationale: Drum mutes are a performance tool, not part of the pattern: a loaded or new project starts with every sound playing.

nodes.label: Recording and overdub
nodes.rationale: Notes go to the nearest step as you heard it: the ~12 ms key-to-sound latency is taken back.

nodes.label: Held notes and legato recording (POLY / MONO)
nodes.rationale: 2.7-2.8.3: on POLY tracks held notes go on under new notes (up to 4 a step); on MONO/LEGATO a note over a held one records legato; screen hints MONO: SET VOICE POLY.

nodes.label: QUANT off (keep your timing)
nodes.rationale: Timing offset becomes the step's nudge so the groove is kept while staying editable step by step.

nodes.label: Free take (loop follows you)
nodes.rationale: The loop length sets the tempo; within 3% the set tempo is kept.

nodes.label: Metronome and click
nodes.rationale: The click is never recorded; the count-in always clicks.

nodes.label: Swing
nodes.rationale: Track swing adds to the global swing; triplet divisions are never swung.

nodes.label: EDIT layer (erase)
nodes.rationale: Erase is MPC-style: hold a key while playing to erase it from every step the playhead passes; all knob turns of one EDIT hold count as one undo.

nodes.label: SEQ layer (steps)
nodes.rationale: A held step edited with a knob is kept when let go; only a plain tap clears.

nodes.label: REV THROW / ECHO THROW
nodes.rationale: Throws never change the song's REV values; nothing is saved or recorded.

nodes.label: The step sequencer
nodes.rationale: Tracks of different lengths loop on their own and stay in phase (polymeters).

nodes.label: Per-step sheet (OCT+ held: SLIDE, NUDGE, FILL, MOVE, COPY, DELETE, RATCHET)
nodes.rationale: 2.8.1: shown as a strip along the bottom so the piano roll stays visible; same sheet on the DRUMS grid.

nodes.label: Parameter locks
nodes.rationale: Elektron-style per-step values, 24 per track; arp, key/scale/chord, voice mode and global pages are not lockable.

nodes.label: Fill conditions (FILL ONLY / NO FILL)
nodes.rationale: One finger brings the fill in and out on the bar: rolls/crashes FILL ONLY, main hat NO FILL.

nodes.label: Chord mode (one finger, one chord)
nodes.rationale: Every chord is built from the scale so it always fits the song; with SCALE CHR chords come from minor.

nodes.label: VLEAD (voice leading)
nodes.rationale: Each chord voiced nearest the last so a progression moves smoothly instead of jumping.

nodes.label: Mute and solo (GLO + keys 1-8)
nodes.rationale: A muted track fades out in a few ms and its pattern runs on in time; several solos add up.

nodes.label: GO values (two-click confirm)
nodes.rationale: One click arms (AGAIN: ...), a second within ~1.5 s acts: guards destructive actions.

nodes.label: Favourites (FAV)
nodes.rationale: Favourites are an FM-1 setting, not part of a project or editor backup.

nodes.label: Working loop
nodes.rationale: The working loop is apart from sections A-D: LOAD copies a section into it, SAVE copies it into a section; the FM-1 holds one song.

nodes.label: TRACKS screen
nodes.rationale: 2.8: a coloured A-D badge shows which section is playing.

nodes.label: KNOB ACCEL (knob acceleration)
nodes.rationale: After JIANT FM: slow turn fine-tunes, fast turn sweeps wider; LEVEL and PAN glide ~3 ms to avoid zipper.

nodes.label: The lights (button and key LEDs)
nodes.rationale: LIGHTS let labels be read in the dark (unreadable unlit on a black FM-1).

nodes.label: The visualiser (12 styles)
nodes.rationale: Sees the mix as if MASTER were full up and costs the sound nothing.

nodes.label: 2ND CORE (dual-core audio)
nodes.rationale: Dual-core audio doubles CPU headroom; 2.8.3 checks every job and falls back to one core instead of crashing if the second core misreads under load.

nodes.label: Arpeggiator
nodes.rationale: 2.7: while the arp runs, loading another sound keeps the arp; a sound's own unchanged arp goes with it.

nodes.label: KBD HOLD (latch without arp)
nodes.rationale: Projects saved before 2.7 open with HOLD OFF when their arp is OFF, so nothing hangs by surprise.

nodes.label: The sound bank (153 factory sounds)
nodes.rationale: All factory sounds are level-matched; browsed by kind; changing a sound never changes key, chord mode, pattern or mix.

nodes.label: SAMPLE engine (sampler)
nodes.rationale: SAMPLE sets are CC0 recordings coloured like a record through an old sampler.

nodes.label: FM6 engine (6-op FM, DX7)
nodes.rationale: msfa (Dexed core) as ported by Felucca 1.0; the eight EDIT values are macros on top of the patch.

nodes.label: PHYS engine (physical models)
nodes.rationale: DaisySP and Rings models as Felucca 1.0 ported them.

nodes.label: Polyphony (voice pool)
nodes.rationale: 8-voice pool shared by synth tracks, drums have their own 6; oldest sounding voice is taken.

nodes.label: DX7 / SysEx patches (FM6 bank)
nodes.rationale: A project keeps the track's PTCH, not the patch: store an edited patch in the bank to keep it.

nodes.label: Master limiter
nodes.rationale: 2.6 look-ahead of one block (0.7 ms) so a loud hit is turned down before it reaches the soft clipper.

nodes.label: Punch-in effects (27)
nodes.rationale: Loops and gate are locked to the tempo and start on the grid; effect lets go cleanly on release.

nodes.label: Black-key punch-in effects (KILL LOW/MID/HIGH, REWIND, OCT UP, FLANGER, AUTO-PAN, FREEZE, LOOP 8T, MONO, FADE OUT)
Punch-in fade (FX + SELECT)
nodes.rationale: 2.8: 0 (instant, anti-click only) to 15 (~0.37 s) so effects ease in and out instead of snapping.

nodes.label: Recorded punch-in FX automation (2.8.5)
nodes.rationale: Pocket-operator style: effects played while REC is on are written into the loop and replay each pass; one effect at a time, 1/16 grid, up to four bars, stored with sections.

nodes.label: FX flush (FX + REC)
nodes.rationale: Pocket-operator FX 16 idea: a punch-in that removes effects; while recording it writes effects off to wipe recorded FX.

nodes.label: TEXTURE (looping bed)
nodes.rationale: A looping bed (vinyl, tape, rain...) as the glue of lo-fi and ambient without taking a track; generated sources use no memory.

nodes.label: Per-track filter
nodes.rationale: 2.8: the drum track has it too.

nodes.label: INSERT (per-track insert effect)
nodes.rationale: After Felucca 1.5; TYPE OFF or MIX 0 costs nothing.

nodes.label: MIDI
nodes.rationale: Bluetooth MIDI is not supported: SLOOP never switches the radio on.

nodes.label: MIDI channels (CH1-CH4)
nodes.rationale: Two tracks never share a channel: a taken channel moves on to the next free one.

nodes.label: MIDI IN / OTHER / OUT settings
nodes.rationale: Notes that came in are never sent back (no MIDI loop).

nodes.label: CLOCK OUT (MIDI clock master)
nodes.rationale: Works only with SYNC = INT: an FM-1 following a clock never sends one (no loop through a computer).

nodes.label: AUDIO CLK (audio sync click)
nodes.rationale: Drives Volca / Pocket Operator / LSDJ SYNC IN over a plain 3.5 mm cable, no MIDI-to-sync box; pulses only while playing so the slave does not creep.

nodes.label: MIDI clock / SYNC
nodes.rationale: 2.8: incoming tempo averaged over the last beats so a steady 140 no longer wavers, while a real tempo change is taken at once.

nodes.label: Bank Select (CC 0)
nodes.rationale: Reaches presets past the 128 Program Change range.

nodes.label: USB RATE
nodes.rationale: 44.1 KHZ only fixes phones that record the FM-1 distorted: the phone converts the rate itself.

nodes.label: Sample loop modes (ONE SHOT, LOOP, LOOP+TAIL)
nodes.rationale: Loop points snap to the nearest zero crossing so the loop does not click; takes no extra memory.

nodes.label: Offline editor and installable app
nodes.rationale: On Android use the app: Chrome on Android does not allow MIDI in a downloaded file.

nodes.label: LIVE page (editor)
nodes.rationale: Its buttons go through the FM-1's own code so device and page always agree.

nodes.label: Scenes (LIVE page)
nodes.rationale: Sections change what plays (notes); scenes change how it sounds (knobs), with morph and crossfader.

nodes.label: Backup and restore
nodes.rationale: A damaged file is refused before writing; each object written as a save writes it so a cut-off restore never leaves half an object.

nodes.label: Going back to official firmware (M-UPGRADE)
nodes.rationale: 2.8 removed the in-browser return-to-stock because it was not reliable on every system; use M-UPGRADE (or Clipper's installer).

hyperedges.label: Master bus chain (texture, DUST, punch-ins, FILT, limiter)
